title: Stamp 2: Bunuel and Latin American Cinema
welcome_lead: Stamp the heritage of Bunuel and modern Latin American directors.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on Bunuel, Cuaron, and Hispanic cinema heritage.

concepts.def: Spanish-Mexican director (1900-1983); surrealist pioneer with Un perro andaluz (1929).
1929 surrealist short film co-written with Salvador Dali.
Mexican director of Y tu mama tambien (2001), Roma (2018, Oscar-winning).
Mexican director of El laberinto del fauno (2006), magical realism on screen.
Auteur cinema; films where the director's vision is central.
Major Spanish-speaking film festival held annually in Donostia-San Sebastian.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bunuel began in surrealist Paris (Un perro andaluz, L'Age d'or), worked in Mexico (Los olvidados, 1950), and returned to Europe for late masterpieces like El discreto encanto de la burguesia (1972).
Cuaron, del Toro, and Inarritu — the 'Three Amigos' — have transformed Hispanic presence in Hollywood, sweeping multiple Best Director Oscars in the 2010s.
Concha de Oro = Golden Shell, top San Sebastian prize. El estreno = premiere. El largometraje = feature film. El cortometraje = short film.
